dna.fixture_why: The artifact stands as the whole ladder by default, which is what it is for. The SWEEP must see one rung at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an all-rungs view in the same spec frames every single rung against a row several times its width and photographs it as a speck. That is not a hypothetical - it crashed the critic on a subject box too small to sample.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 51.2% of frame width and 20.8% of its height, with a subject share of 5.43%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.27. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

octave_stack.description: The same noise field at one, two, three, four and six octaves, with every octave also drawn alone at its true amplitude. The contributions halve, so the ladder converges before anything is rendered - and four of the family's eight members offer a sixth rung.
